Full proceedings paper and method definitions.

artifact.version_note: Official NIPS 2017 proceedings PDF; title and both authors checked.

contexts.evidence: Section 4.1 (pp. 5–6) derives KernelSHAP as weighted linear regression over simplified inputs, supporting its inclusion among perturbation/surrogate methods.
Sections 4.1–4.2 (pp. 5–7) distinguish model-agnostic KernelSHAP from model-specific methods including Deep SHAP; SHAP generally is not restricted to black-box use.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Shapley-value methods such as KernelSHAP \parencite{LundbergLee2017} play a \emph{different}, cooperative game over input coalitions in a black-box setting, complementary to the white-box backward game here.

contexts.evidence: Section 4 defines SHAP through conditional-expectation coalitions; Section 4.1 supplies black-box KernelSHAP, while Section 4.2 uses network internals for Deep SHAP.
contexts.proposed_replacement: KernelSHAP frames explanation as a cooperative game over feature coalitions~\parencite{LundbergLee2017} in a \emph{black-box} setting; it is therefore a distinct, complementary game that explains marginal input-feature contributions relative to a baseline, whereas our backward game explains how relevance is routed through network internals in a \emph{white-box} setting.

contexts.evidence: Section 4.1 (pp. 5–6) supports the cited classification as perturbation/surrogate explanation. The paper does not establish the thesis’s subsequent structural-loss claim.
Section 4.1 and Theorem 2 (pp. 5–6) derive the model-agnostic weighted-regression estimator. SLIC superpixels describe the thesis implementation, not a claim of this source.

notes: The proceedings metadata leaves pages empty; no substantive bibliographic correction is needed. SHAP is a framework that includes model-specific approximations; KernelSHAP is model-agnostic.

contexts.evidence: Example 3.25, p. 93, identifies log-sum-exp and negative entropy on the simplex as conjugates and gives the normalized-exponential optimizer; Section 3.3 scaling yields temperature theta.
Example 3.25, p. 93, together with conjugate scaling on p. 95 yields the stated entropy-regularized maximum and Gibbs optimizer.
Example 3.25, p. 93, and Section 3.3 (pp. 94–95) supply entropy/log-sum-exp conjugacy, biconjugacy and scaling. Strict concavity on the simplex gives uniqueness.
This is the weighted form of Example 3.25, p. 93: replace rewards by r_i + log(bar pi_i) on the prior support. Expanding the two KL terms verifies the displayed identity.
